operation.description: Compute the row-by-column product of two compatible symbolic matrices over one explicitly ordered rational-function field. Every product entry is returned as a canonical reduced rational function; admission bounds unreduced expansion plus cancellation-safe canonical and aggregate support, exponents, coefficients, and result before SymPy multiplication.

examples.description: Multiply [[a, b]] by the column [[1], [1]] over QQ(a, b); both matrices must use the same ordered field and compatible inner dimension.
examples.name: symbolic_matrix_product

CanonicalRational.description: A reduced rational whose denominator is positive and whose zero is 0/1.

den.description: Positive canonical decimal denominator; together with num it must be reduced, and integers use den='1'.
den.title: Den

num.description: Canonical decimal numerator of the reduced rational.
num.title: Num

CanonicalRational.title: CanonicalRational

RationalFunction.description:
One reduced element of ``QQ(t_1, ..., t_n)``.

The denominator is monic and the numerator and denominator are coprime.
This makes the sparse representation unique for the declared variable
order.  With no variables, the value is a canonical rational represented
by one constant numerator over the constant denominator one.
RationalFunction.title: RationalFunction

terms.description: Nonzero monomials in descending lexicographic order of their exponent tuples (highest first). For one variable, list [2] before [0].
terms.title: Terms

SymbolicMatrix.description:
One nonempty rectangular matrix over a multivariate rational-function field.

Every entry is a canonical reduced numerator/denominator value over the
declared ordered variables. For example, the former expression ``a*c`` is
represented by one numerator term with exponents ``(1, 0, 1, ...)`` and a
unit denominator; ``f/e`` is represented by numerator ``f`` and denominator
``e``. This preserves every element of ``QQ(t_1, ..., t_n)`` without parsing
caller text with SymPy.
SymbolicMatrix.title: SymbolicMatrix

input_schema.description: Two compatible symbolic matrices whose exact product is representable.

left.description: A nonempty symbolic matrix over QQ(t_1, ..., t_n). Its ordered field variables must exactly match right.variables.

right.description: A nonempty symbolic matrix over the same ordered field as left. Its row count must equal left's column count.

terms.title: Terms

output_schema.description:
One nonempty rectangular matrix over a multivariate rational-function field.

Every entry is a canonical reduced numerator/denominator value over the
declared ordered variables. For example, the former expression ``a*c`` is
represented by one numerator term with exponents ``(1, 0, 1, ...)`` and a
unit denominator; ``f/e`` is represented by numerator ``f`` and denominator
``e``. This preserves every element of ``QQ(t_1, ..., t_n)`` without parsing
caller text with SymPy.
output_schema.title: SymbolicMatrix
